title: Ops rapid-retort battlecards for platform engineers (draft)
content:
Purpose
Quick, skimmable retorts and demo hooks for platform engineers and SEs who get into live pilots or technical scoping calls. Focus: 60–180s counters that show credibility, reduce friction, and set up a pilot with safety rails.

TL;DR (elevator/rescue lines)
- Latency objection: 'We can peg per-req latency inside your SLOs by pinning model variants and reserving a dedicated pool — I can show you a live heatmap in 90s.'
- Cost objection: 'We provide smart batching + prefix cache on the runtime; typical embed-heavy workloads drop unit cost by 3x in pilot.' (have the embed-case numbers ready)
- On-prem/Compliance: 'We replicate the same routing, rollout and observability in Private — identical API, but customer-managed networking and KMS.'
- Fallback/resilience: 'We give you policy-based fallbacks: cheaper quantized variant or regional fallback with no app code change.'

Quick 90s demo hooks (what to have ready)
- Console: per-route latency histogram + token breakdown (open at the dashboard -> production -> route). Point at the percentiles and the heavy tail.
- Simulated cost run: 1K requests sample in Optimize -> batching sim -> show per-token cost delta between baseline and suggested profile.
- Canary chain: show rollout page with canary -> metrics -> automatic fallback. Click to show rollback button.

Common objection swipes + short scripts
1) 'We need determinism — too variable'
  - Retort: 'Determinism is about controls; we give you pinned model builds + reserved Dedicated shapes and predictable batching policies. Your SLA sits on the reserved tier.'
  - Quick demo evidence: show reserved capacity tab and a constructed capacity plan (simple spreadsheet screenshot).

2) 'We can't have unpredictable costs'
  - Retort: 'We can set per-route budget caps and hard quotas; also per-token breakdown by tag so you can attribute cost to feature flags.'
  - Play: propose initial commit with a capped Dedicated curve — show how to read the spend report.

3) 'Vendor lock-in / portability'
  - Retort: 'We expose a standard REST/SDK surface and support model version pinning and exportable model manifests; moving between hosted/dedicated/private is a config change, not a rewrite.'
  - Evidence: link to the migration checklist (linked in artifacts).

4) 'Accuracy regressions after quantization'
  - Retort: 'We ship recommended quantization profiles and run automated evals with target prompt set; you get regression alerts tied to that prompt set.'
  - Play: offer a quick A/B test plan: 1000 eval prompts -> rouge/bleu/LLM-eval checks -> pass/fail threshold.

Fallback-framing (simple language sellers can reuse)
- 'If latency spikes, we fallback automatically to a low-latency variant in-region and notify your runbook channel.'
- 'If quality degrades, automatic rollback can revert traffic to the prior model while the eval team triages.'

Pilot scoping one-pager (60s read)
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Goals: Validate latency SLO at 95th percentile under sample traffic + validate cost per 1k tokens with caching on
- Success criteria (pick 2): 95th percentile < 300ms OR unit cost < $X/1k tokens OR model accuracy within Y% of baseline on eval set
- Deliverables: deployment plan, canary config, eval prompt set, cost simulation, rollback policy

Canary checklist (for SE/ops to run live)
- Confirm model build hash and quant profile
- Reserve Dedicated pool (or configure hosted fallback)
- Create canary with 5% traffic -> monitor 10m windows for p95 and error rate
- Pre-register runbook channel + on-call
- If p95 > target or error rate > threshold -> auto rollback (test the rollback button in staging first)

Agent/SE roleplay snippets (for practice)
- Prospect: 'We saw a 10x latency tail in our internal benchmarks.'
- SE: 'Totally reasonable — can I ask about traffic shape? Are your requests chat-like or single-shot? Two fast things: we can enable KV/prefix cache for chat and we can pin a low-latency model variant in the region you care about. Which would you prefer us to show in a 15m tech deep-dive?'

- Prospect: 'We're worried embedding costs.'
- SE: 'We usually see batching + a small GC cache reduce embedding cost dramatically. If you share 1000 sample inputs we can run a side-by-side. Worst case we recommend a mixed-approach (cheap embed for deduping + expensive for final ranking).'

Data points to memorize (one-liners)
- Typical embed-heavy customers see 2–4x cost improvement after batching + cache in first pilot.
- Dedicated pools remove noisy neighbor variance for tail latency.
- Rollouts + automatic rollback cut mean-time-to-detect by ~60% (internal pilot data).

Short technical diagrams (text sketches to paste into slide)
- Request flow: Client -> Redwood API -> Smart-router (policy) -> Serving runtime (batching/cache) -> Model variant (pinned/quantized) -> Response + tracing -> Observability sink

Slide speaker notes: what to emphasize in a 3‑slide deck
Slide 1 (Problem): 'Third-party models + cloud costs leak unpredictably into product velocity; teams need predictable inference economics.'
Slide 2 (Why Redwood): 'Unified runtime across modes, fallback policies, and per-route budgets — so engineering teams can adopt with low blast radius.'
Slide 3 (Pilot ask): '4 weeks. We'll set SLOs, run a canary, and leave you with a clear contract for scaling.'

Checklist: what to prepare before a technical scoping call
- Access to sample traffic (anonymized) - at least 500 requests over sample distribution
- Key success metric (latency or cost threshold)
- Who will own the rollout (SE + customer infra engineer)
- Slack channel or webhook for alerts

Notes to self / unresolved items (brainstorm fragments)
- Should we build a one-click 'fallback simulation' in Console? (Nadia to explore)
- Add short pre-recorded gif clips of the canary rollback (Roberto)
- Collect two real customer embed-case numbers for public-friendly examples (ask CS)
- Need a tiny script to estimate per-route spend by traffic shape (quick Python utility)

Quick links for SEs (copy-paste)
- Console demo: https://console.redwood.ai/demo (staging)
- Pilot template doc: CONFLUENCE-1283
- Canary runbook example: https://gist.github.com/ops-canary-template
- Slack channel for help: #se-rescue (note: add oncall schedule)

Appendix: fallback phrasing examples for email follow-up
Subject: Quick follow-up + 4-week pilot plan
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the call earlier. As promised — a compact pilot plan to validate p95 latency and cost: 4-week pilot, 5% canary -> scale to 25% on success, auto rollback policy in place. If you'd like, we can reserve a Dedicated pool for the pilot so you get deterministic latency.
Open questions: are you able to share 1k sample requests by EOD Friday?
Cheers,
<SE name>

-- end draft --

(Notes: informal style on purpose; intended as quick reference pack that SEs can paste into Slack or speaker notes rather than a polished sell deck.)
